title: Proper acyclicity of injectives extended from an arbitrary Cartesian open
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $p:V\to T$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism], let $i:W\hookrightarrow T$ be an arbitrary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and put $U=V\times_TW$, with projections $k:U\hookrightarrow V$ and $r:U\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use sheaves of modules over the constant sheaves of rings $A_H$ on the small pro-etale sites of $H=U,V,W,T$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $p_*,r_*$ and $i^*,k^*$ for direct image and exact inverse image with constant-ring identifications [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and $i_!,k_!$ for extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero].
Assume that there is an integer $d\geq0$ such that $R^qp_*F=0$ for every module sheaf $F$ on $V$ and every $q>d$. For every injective object $J$ of the module category on $U$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], its extension $k_!J$ is $p_*$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic]:
$$R^qp_*(k_!J)=0\qquad(q>0).$$
Here $R^qp_*F=\mathcal H^q(Rp_*(F[0]))$ uses the ordinary uncompleted derived direct image and cohomology sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. No quasi-compactness of $i$ and no etale-origin condition on $J$ is assumed.

source.place: Steps 2–4: the injective-acyclicity input for deriving proper/open support on the whole pro-etale category; agent-extracted pro-etale sheaf obligation, not a theorem asserted by the etale source. Etale analogue: literature/stacks-project/more-etale.tex, Tag 0F7B, label lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, case (b). Pro-etale open functors: proetale.tex, Tag 09AE, label definition-extension-zero; Tag 09BN, label lemma-open-immersion.

proof.text:
Put $F=k_!J$. We first record an evaluation identity, valid for any sheaf $G$ on $V$ and any affine weakly contractible object $Q\to T$. Choose a bounded-below injective resolution $G\to I^\bullet$: the small constant-ring module category is Grothendieck with enough injectives by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] supplies a bounded-below injective representative. It computes the ordinary $Rp_*G$ by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Evaluation at $Q$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-wcontractible-affine-evaluation-colimits]. For $P=V\times_TQ$, the morphism $P\to V$ is weakly etale by base-change stability in [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change], and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives] says that restricting $I^\bullet$ to $P$ remains an injective resolution. The direct-image section formula therefore gives
$$ (R^qp_*G)(Q)=H^q((p_*I^\bullet)(Q))=H^q(I^\bullet(P))=H^q(P,G|_P). $$
This is an identity of module groups, with no appeal to geometric-point stalks. For a proper morphism $h:Y\to Q$ and a sheaf $M$ on $Y$, choose a bounded-below injective resolution $M\to K^\bullet$. The direct-image formula at the terminal object is $(h_*K^\bullet)(Q)=K^\bullet(Y)$. Exact evaluation on $Q_{\mathrm{proet}}$ therefore gives $(R^qh_*M)(Q)=H^q(K^\bullet(Y))=H^q(Y,M)$. Here exact evaluation on $Q_{\mathrm{proet}}$ follows from the slice-site identification in the restriction lemma and the following lifting calculation: $Q$ remains weakly contractible in the slice: a section of a sheaf over the terminal slice object is a map from $h_Q$ over $h_Q$. An epimorphism in that slice is an epimorphism of the underlying sheaves, so weak contractibility lifts this map; the lift is automatically over $h_Q$ because its composite to $h_Q$ is the identity. Thus the exact-evaluation statement applies on $Q_{\mathrm{proet}}$ as well.

source.place: Tag 0946, label lemma-w-contractible, (1); derived.tex Tag 05TI, label lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived; proetale.tex Tag 09AE and localized-site restriction; explicit injective-resolution calculation

proof.text: Fix such a $Q=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Put $W_Q=W\times_TQ$, $U_Q=U\times_TQ$, $P=V\times_TQ$, and denote the induced maps by $p_Q:P\to Q$ and $k_Q:U_Q\hookrightarrow P$. Properness and the open-immersion assertions follow from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. The map $U_Q\to U$ is weakly etale by base-change stability in [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]; hence $J_Q=J|_{U_Q}$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives]. Write $g:P\to V$ and $g_U:U_Q\to U$ for the projections; both are weakly etale, so $P$ and $U_Q$ are objects of $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$. For such a map the inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is restriction: for an object $Y\to P$ of $P_{\mathrm{proet}}$, an object $(Z,\phi:Y\to P\times_VZ)$ of the index category $\mathcal I_Y$ is the same as a $V$-morphism $Y\to Z$, where $Y$ lies over $V$ through $Y\to P\to V$ (weakly etale by composition, [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]); hence $(Y\to V,\ (\mathrm{id}_Y,Y\to P))$ is initial in $\mathcal I_Y$, the presheaf colimit is $F(Y\to V)=(F|_P)(Y)$ naturally in $Y$, and this is already a sheaf, so sheafification changes nothing. The structure map $g^{-1}A_V\to A_P$ is the identity on constant sections, which is the identification of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] (2), so the module pullback is $g^{-1}$ itself. Thus $g^*F\cong F|_P$ and likewise $g_U^*J\cong J|_{U_Q}=J_Q$. Applied to the Cartesian square of $k$ and $g$ (note $U\times_VP=U\times_TQ=U_Q$), [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] gives $g^{-1}k_!J\cong k_{Q!}g_U^{-1}J$, i.e. identifies $F|_P$ with $k_{Q!}J_Q$. Let $S=\{b\in B:D(b)\subseteq W_Q\}$. Index by the small nonempty directed poset of finite subsets $E\subseteq S$, ordered by inclusion, and set $W_E=\bigcup_{b\in E}D(b)$ and $U_E=P\times_QW_E$. Principal opens form a basis directly from the Zariski definition: the complement of $V(I)$ is $\bigcup_{b\in I}D(b)$. Thus $W_Q=\bigcup_EW_E$ and $U_Q=\bigcup_EU_E$; the union of two finite subsets is an upper bound. For any affine open $L\subseteq Q$, the restriction of $D(b)$ is $D(b|_L)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] this is the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(\Gamma(L,\mathcal O_L)_{b|_L})$, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. A finite union of quasi-compact subsets is quasi-compact: extract a finite subcover on each subset and take their finite union. Thus $W_E\hookrightarrow Q$ is quasi-compact by the affine-preimage definition in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The map $k_E:U_E\hookrightarrow P$ is quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change]. The restricted map $r_E:U_E\to W_E$ is proper by the proper-base-change lemma. The open immersion $a_E:U_E\hookrightarrow U_Q$ is a weakly etale localization with the same restricted constant ring by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Finally $J_E=J_Q|_{U_E}$ is injective by the restriction lemma. The index $E=\varnothing$ gives the empty open and the zero sheaf, which is injective.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-proetale-open-injective-proper-acyclic] to $B=P$, $D=Q$, $C=U_E$, $E=W_E$, $p=p_Q$, $r=r_E$, and the two quasi-compact open immersions just constructed. Both vertical maps are proper, $p_Qk_E=i_Er_E$, the coefficients are the same finite commutative ring $A$, and $J_E$ is an injective on the small pro-etale site. It gives $R^qp_{Q,*}(k_{E!}J_E)=0$ for every $q>0$. Set $F_E=k_{E!}J_E$. The evaluation identity of Step 1, now with base $Q$ and its terminal object, gives $H^q(P,F_E)=0$ for every $E$ and $q>0$. This uses the pro-etale statement of the cited node, not the etale analogue in Stacks Tag 0F7B.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, label lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, motivates the proper/open injective reduction only; the required pro-etale quasi-compact assertion is the existing DAG obligation lem-sp-proetale-open-injective-proper-acyclic

proof.text:
Write $a_E:U_E\hookrightarrow U_Q$. For $E\subseteq E'$, the open-adjunction counit on $U_{E'}$ gives the transition $a_{E!}J_E\to a_{E'!}J_{E'}$ after extension to $U_Q$. Under the Hom adjunction of [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction], these transitions correspond to restriction of maps from $J_Q$: restrictions from $U_{E^{\prime\prime}}$ to $U_{E^{\prime}}$ and then $U_E$ compose to direct restriction to $U_E$. The adjunction bijection thus proves both the identity and composition laws for the transitions, so they form a diagram. Its cocone to $J_Q$ exhibits
$$ \varinjlim_E a_{E!}J_E\cong J_Q. $$
Indeed, by that adjunction a compatible family of maps $a_{E!}J_E\to N$ is exactly a compatible family $J_Q|_{U_E}\to N|_{U_E}$. It glues uniquely to a map $J_Q\to N$: on an arbitrary object of $U_Q$ use its open cover by inverse images of the $U_E$ and the sheaf gluing axiom; this is a pro-etale covering because its maps are open immersions, and on each affine open the Zariski cover has a finite refinement by affine opens; agreements on overlaps follow by passing to $E\cup E'$. Thus the cocone has the colimit universal property. The small colimits exist by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Applying the left adjoint $k_{Q!}$ preserves this colimit, as follows by applying its Hom adjunction to the colimit universal property. Also $k_{Q!}a_{E!}\cong k_{E!}$, since both have right adjoint $a_E^*k_Q^*=k_E^*$. Consequently
$$ F|_P\cong k_{Q!}J_Q\cong\varinjlim_E F_E. $$
All these maps are the maps induced by the open counits, so this is a colimit of the same coefficient sheaves used in Step 3.

source.place: Tag 09AE, label definition-extension-zero; the open-cover gluing and two adjunction universal-property calculations are written out here

proof.text:
The morphism $p_Q:P\to Q$ is proper, hence separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Because $Q$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] gives that $P$ is a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Its identity morphism makes $P$ the terminal object of $P_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Apply [det-pe-bounded-continuity-sections] with $X=P$, its terminal object $P$, ring sheaf $A_P$, and the diagram of complexes $F_E[0]$. The index of finite subsets is small and filtered, all complexes vanish below the common bound $0$, and the terminal object is qcqs. Step 4 identifies the termwise colimit with $(F|_P)[0]$. Thus, for every $q>0$,
$$ H^q(P,F|_P)\cong\varinjlim_E H^q(P,F_E)=0 $$
by Step 3. The continuity node allows an arbitrary sheaf of rings and all module sheaves, so neither rational coefficients nor an etale-origin condition is being imposed.

proof.text: For every $q>0$ and every affine weakly contractible $Q\to T$, Steps 1 and 5 give $(R^qp_*k_!J)(Q)=0$. Clause (i) of [lem-sf-proetale-vanishing-detection] therefore gives $R^qp_*k_!J=0$ as a module sheaf on the whole small pro-etale site. This proves the stated acyclicity. The finite cohomological-dimension hypothesis is retained in the statement; this reduction does not use it because the existing quasi-compact-open acyclicity node is stronger and itself imposes no such bound. The geometric pro-etale acyclicity obligation remains in that existing node rather than being claimed from the etale source.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q11-adbac5a06 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 21 cited nodes and the current blueprint proof prop-exc-base-change-proper.proof.md. The statement is identical to the side-DAG copy, so the target is not weakened. The finite-cd hypothesis is kept but not used. No new nodes. There is no cycle: the item does not appear among its dependencies' 905 transitive dependencies. The split is a real reduction, not a restatement. Step 1 evaluates at an affine weakly contractible Q (exact evaluation, restriction of injectives, direct-image section formula). Step 2 exhausts W_Q by finite unions of principal opens; these are quasi-compact over affine Q, k_E is quasi-compact by base change and r_E is proper.
